body.statement: Assume \(p\geq3\) and fix the ordered injection \(\iota:\{X,Y,Z\}\hookrightarrow\{1,\ldots,p\}\). If \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\) and every recovered component law belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CPCM}}\), then the pooled-law tuple identifies each labeled type graph \(D_r\). If the recovered law belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathfrak G,\Theta,q)\), it also identifies the \(\iota\)-indexed contrast vector \(\boldsymbol\tau=((\tau_{i_Y,r},\tau_{i_Z,r}))_{r=1}^{K}\) through the displayed truncated factorization at \(V_{i_X}\).
body.justification: This transfers the acquisition certificate to causal structure and supported intervention quantities.
body.gap: Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin identifies CPCM graphs from direct laws, Gao--Cai--Hara identifies PT-SEM DAGs and thinning parameters from direct count vectors, and Luo--Sun--Zhang Section 4.2 studies functional consistency under linear aggregation and gives affine ANM/PNL consequences; Section 4.3 concerns conditional-independence consistency. Known labeled multi-composition pools remain outside its target, and none of these results recovers labeled causal laws through several independent known-composition mixtures.
body.consumer: It defines what a successful known-composition prospective bulk assay identifies at the cellular causal level.
body.proof_tex:
Full column rank and the rank-frontier theorem first identify each labeled component law \(P_r\) from the pooled-law tuple.  This is an equality between the causal model's observational law and the observable recovery functional, not a definition of a causal effect.

For a recovered \(P_r\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CPCM}}\), causal sufficiency and pairwise identifiability are part of the class definition.  The cited CPCM DAG-identification lemma therefore implies that its labeled generating graph \(D_r\) is the unique CPCM DAG compatible with \(P_r\).  Applying this separately to the labeled columns of \(M\) identifies the entire graph tuple.

Now suppose the recovered model lies in
\(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathfrak G,\Theta,q)\).  By polynomial-class inclusion it has full support.  Hence, for every parent configuration,
\[
p_{rs}(v_s\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)})
=\frac{\Pr_{P_r}(V_s=v_s,\,
V_{\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}=v_{\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)})}
{\Pr_{P_r}(V_{\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}
=v_{\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)})} \tag{15}
\]
is an identified ratio with a strictly positive denominator.  Independent exogenous variables give modular structural assignments.  Replacing the equation for \(V_{i_X}\) by the constant \(x\) therefore deletes precisely its observational factor, while the remaining kernels are unchanged.  Successive summation in a topological order proves that
\[
P_r^{\operatorname{do}(V_{i_X}=x)}(v_{-i_X})
=\prod_{s\ne i_X}
p_{rs}(v_s\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)})
\big|_{v_{i_X}=x} \tag{16}
\]
is normalized.  This is the standard truncated-factorization consequence of the structural model, and proves its equality to the causal intervention law rather than stipulating that equality as the estimand.

Finally, Poisson conditional moments are polynomials in their rates.  Induction in topological order, with the positive-polynomial rates, shows that all polynomial moments in (16) are finite for the fixed interventions \(x=1,2\).  Thus the two expectations in each contrast exist.  Equations (15)--(16), followed by the two indicated summations and subtraction, are an observable functional of the recovered law and graph and equal the causal target.  Hence the pooled-law tuple identifies \(\boldsymbol\tau\).
